summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old pregnant woman with a history of bipolar disorder and prior psychiatric hospitalizations was admitted for a manic episode with psychotic features, presenting with auditory hallucinations concerning harm to her fetus. She had no obstetric complications, and fetal monitoring remained reassuring throughout. She was evaluated by psychiatry, restarted on haloperidol, and treated for agitation with lorazepam and supportive care, including IV fluids for mild dehydration. Her symptoms improved significantly, and due to her psychiatric history and ongoing risk, she was transferred to an inpatient psychiatric facility for continued medication management and stabilization. She was discharged in stable mental and physical condition with a clear plan for follow-up care.
